# HEN Morning Analysis — 2026-10-29
**Hunt Energy Network | ERCOT BESS Fleet (32 Nodes)**
*Prepared for Trading Desk & Asset Management | DA Offer Deadline: 10:00 AM CT*

---

## 1. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY

Yesterday's fleet average RT settled at **$50.18/MWh**, up from $42.30 on 10-26 and continuing the three-day ascending trend (10-25: $22.01 → 10-26: $42.30 → 10-27: $57.76), though yesterday's count of spike nodes (10) represents a partial recovery from the extreme 10-26 event (32 nodes) and a moderation from 10-27 (11 nodes). The standout RT performers were concentrated in the West and South Texas corridors: **CEDRVALE_RN** led with RT exceeding DA by **$75.16/MWh**, followed by **SANDLAKE_RN** ($73.82 RT premium), **COYOTSPR_RN** and **FAULKNER_RN** (both $63.85), and **RTLSNAKE_BT** ($58.39) — all nodes where RT dispatch would have meaningfully outperformed any DA commitment. Conversely, the **TOYAH_RN**, **GOMZ_RN**, and **RUSSEKST_RN** nodes posted negative RT prices, making them the best candidates for DA commitment capture, with TOYAH holding the top positive DART at **+$13.79/MWh** (DA premium over RT). Congestion was the dominant structural driver: the **BLESSING_1382** constraint alone bound for **21 of 24 hours** with a peak shadow price of **$409.87/MWh** at HE14, while **BLESSI_PAVLOV1_1** ran 12 hours at a peak of $331.14/MWh — creating sharply divergent nodal outcomes across the fleet and rewarding nodes on the favorable side of these constraints (notably PAVLOV_BT_RN at +$133.84/MWh MCC benefit and JUNCTION_RN at +$77.88/MWh).

---

## 2. DISPATCH STRATEGY BY NODE

**🔵 LEAN DA — Commit in Day-Ahead:**
JUNCTION_RN (Sharpe +0.346, avg DART +$3.26, MCC +$77.88) and TOYAH_RN (Sharpe +0.310, avg DART +$5.47 over 5 days, today's DART +$13.79) are the highest-confidence DA plays in the fleet — both nodes have shown consistent DA premium over RT across 120 hours with positive MCC exposure reinforcing the DA commitment case. HAMI_BESS_RN (Sharpe +0.159) and RUSSEKST_RN (Sharpe +0.156) are mild DA leans with lower conviction; both are exposed to the TREADW_YELWJC1_1 and ESCOND_GANSO1_1 constraints, which provided modest positive MCC support yesterday and may repeat given similar wind patterns.

**🟡 LEAN RT — Dispatch Real-Time:**
The cluster of West/South Texas nodes — **CEDRVALE_RN, SANDLAKE_RN, COYOTSPR_RN, FAULKNER_RN, RTLSNAKE_BT** (all Sharpe -0.45 to -0.46), plus **SBEAN_BESS** and **SADLBACK_RN/LONESTAR_RN** — have demonstrated five-day patterns where RT consistently exceeded DA by $15–$26/MWh on average; yesterday's single-day RT premiums of $58–$75 at these nodes confirm the bias. **MAINLAND_RN** (Sharpe -0.571, avg DART -$13.83, the only STRONG RT node) is the highest-conviction RT dispatch in the fleet and should not be committed in DA absent a compelling AS capture rationale. **PAVLOV_BT_RN** is a special case: Sharpe -0.278 with enormous RT volatility (stdev $73.42) but a remarkable MCC benefit of +$133.84/MWh — this node's RT exposure is high-risk/high-reward and should be evaluated hour-by-hour against real-time constraint status on BLESSI_PAVLOV1_1.

**⚪ NEUTRAL — Monitor, No Edge:**
The 16 neutral nodes (CATARINA_B1, CISC_RN, DIBOL_RN, FALFUR_RN, FRMRSVLW_RN, FTDUNCAN_RN, GOMZ_RN, HOLCOMB_RN1, LFSTH_RN, MNWL_BESS_RN, MV_VALV4_RN, OLNEYTN_RN, PAULN_RN, POTEETS_RN, TYNAN_RN, WLTC_ESR_RN) show no persistent DA-RT edge; default to AS capture or price-responsive RT holding strategy. Note that **FTDUNCAN_RN** carries the only negative MCC in the fleet (-$16.87/MWh) — congestion is working against this node, and any DA energy commitment should be sized conservatively until the BLESSING complex constraints relax.

---

## 3. CONSTRAINT ANALYSIS

| Constraint | Avg Shadow | Peak | Binding Hrs | Peak HE | HEN Nodes | Commercial Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BLESSING_1382 | $125.56/MWh | $409.87/MWh | 21h | HE14 | CATARINA_B1, HOLCOMB_RN1, FTDUNCAN_RN, MV_VALV4_RN | ⚠️ SIGNIFICANT |
| BLESSI_PAVLOV1_1 | $141.33/MWh | $331.14/MWh | 12h | HE04 | CATARINA_B1, HOLCOMB_RN1, FTDUNCAN_RN, MV_VALV4_RN | ⚠️ SIGNIFICANT |
| TREADW_YELWJC1_1 (W→E) | $151.39/MWh | $231.21/MWh | 2h | HE15 | RUSSEKST_RN, CATARINA_B1, HOLCOMB_RN1, JUNCTION_RN | ✅ BENEFIT (select nodes) |
| ASHERT_CATARI1_1 | $66.29/MWh | $163.56/MWh | 3h | HE13 | CATARINA_B1, HOLCOMB_RN1, RUSSEKST_RN, TOYAH_RN | ✅ BENEFIT (select nodes) |
| ESCOND_GANSO1_1 | $51.35/MWh | $51.35/MWh | 1h | HE16 | RUSSEKST_RN, CATARINA_B1, HAMI_BESS_RN, JUNCTION_RN | ✅ BENEFIT (select nodes) |

**BLESSING_1382 & BLESSI_PAVLOV1_1 (Commercially Significant — Flag for Escalation):** These two Blessing-complex constraints are the most impactful in the fleet. BLESSING_1382 bound for **21 of 24 hours** — an extraordinarily persistent constraint — with a peak shadow of $409.87/MWh at HE14 and average of $125.56/MWh. BLESSI_PAVLOV1_1 added 12 hours of binding at avg $141.33/MWh peaking at $331.14 at HE04. Both constraints expose the same four HEN nodes: **CATARINA_B1** (net MCC +$64.58/MWh — congestion benefit), **HOLCOMB_RN1** (+$27.13/MWh — benefit), **MV_VALV4_RN** (+$25.51/MWh — benefit), and critically **FTDUNCAN_RN** (-$16.87/MWh — cost), indicating FTDUNCAN sits on the load-side (or adverse shift factor side) of the Blessing export constraint while the other three nodes benefit. All four MCC values exceed the $10/MWh commercial significance threshold.

**TREADW_YELWJC1_1 (W→E, 2h binding, HE15 peak $163.78/MWh):** This westbound constraint bound briefly at HE15 with the highest avg shadow price in the fleet at $151.39/MWh. JUNCTION_RN (+$77.88 MCC) and RUSSEKST_RN are the primary beneficiaries, consistent with their positive Sharpe ratios — this constraint structurally supports the DA-lean recommendation for both nodes. CATARINA_B1 and HOLCOMB_RN1 also benefit, adding further congestion tailwind to their positive MCC profiles.

**ASHERT_CATARI1_1 (3h, HE13 peak $78.73/MWh):** Binding during the afternoon solar production peak (HE13), this constraint contributes positive MCC to CATARINA_B1, HOLCOMB_RN1, RUSSEKST_RN, and TOYAH_RN — reinforcing the DA commitment case for TOYAH and RUSSEKST, which already carry positive DARTs. Shadow prices here are moderate but the HE13 binding hour aligns with solar ramp-down timing and should be watched for recurrence as cloud cover increases this week.

---

## 4. WEATHER & LOAD OUTLOOK

**Today (10-29):** Near-term weather is the dominant commercial risk. San Antonio (100% precip), Midland (99%), Laredo (87%), and Abilene (63%) are all flagging heavy precipitation — this pattern will suppress solar output across West and South Texas materially, potentially pushing RT prices higher at nodes that benefit from reduced renewable supply. Tomorrow (10-30) intensifies: Lubbock (100%), Midland (100%), Wichita Falls (94%), and Abilene (94%) all show near-certain precipitation, signaling a 2-day window of significantly reduced wind and solar generation across the Permian/Panhandle corridor.

**Load & Renewable Outlook:** With Brownsville/Corpus Christi remaining warm (86–90°F highs through the week) and Houston staying in the low-to-mid 80s, South Texas load will remain supported — no demand destruction from cooling demand in the near term. The combination of suppressed West Texas renewables and sustained coastal load could push fleet-wide RT averages above yesterday's $50.18/MWh, particularly Thursday-Friday when the precipitation system clears and wind ramps back in erratically. By 11/1–11/2, a second precip system tracks through DFW (80% on 11-2) and Waco (49%/79%), extending renewable suppression risk into the first weekend of November.

**Dispatch Implication:** The 2-day precipitation window (10-29 to 10-30) favors RT-bias dispatch at LEAN RT nodes where solar depression tends to tighten the RT stack, while the return of wind and solar on 10-31 through 11-3 may bring negative price risk back to West Texas nodes (consistent with the TOYAH_RN, GOMZ_RN, RUSSEKST_RN negative price pattern). Plan for a potential regime flip at West Texas nodes mid-week: RT favorable today/tomorrow, DA favorable by Thursday.

---

## 5. MODO INDEX CONTEXT

**HEN 2026 vs. Market Benchmark:** HEN's custom index is running at **$20,702/MW/yr** (241 days YTD through 8/28) versus the 1-Hr Without HEN benchmark at **$16,103/MW/yr** — a **$4,599/MW/yr outperformance (+28.6%)** attributable primarily to HEN's RT energy strategy. The HEN index's top contributor is RT energy at **$11,288/MW/yr** (55% of total revenue), more than tripling the benchmark's $3,197 RT contribution, confirming that HEN's RT dispatch bias has been the structural alpha driver YTD.

**Fort Duncan Outperformance:** Fort Duncan is generating **$35,660/MW/yr** vs. the 2-Hr Without Fort Duncan benchmark of $30,985 — a **$4,675/MW/yr premium** driven overwhelmingly by RT energy at **$23,717/MW/yr** (66% of Fort Duncan revenue). This is the strongest RT capture in the portfolio and aligns with the FTDUNCAN_RN appearing in the neutral Sharpe bucket (not yet STRONG RT signal) — suggesting there may be additional DA AS monetization opportunity at this node given the strong benchmark DA energy contribution ($10,553 in the benchmark vs. only $3,755 at Fort Duncan), possibly constrained by the negative MCC exposure noted above.

**Revenue Mix Signal:** The HEN index's ECRS DA contribution of **$1,989/MW/yr** and the benchmark's RRS DA of **$3,002/MW/yr** suggest HEN has tilted away from AS DA capacity toward RT energy — the right call in a high-volatility RT environment, but worth reassessing as the AS DA spread data (see Section 5) shows select hours with repeatable DA premium opportunity.

---

## 6. AS MARKET ANALYSIS (Last 3 Days: 10-26 through 10-28)

**Most Consistent DA Premium:** REGDN is the most stable DA-premium service over the 3-day window, with a 3-day average spread of only **-$0.02/MW** (essentially flat) and a best-hour DA premium of **+$2.27/MW at HE18** (3-day avg) — nearly negligible RT bleed, making it the lowest-risk DA offer service in the current window. **ECRS** improved sharply on 10-28 (-$0.08/MW daily spread) after a volatile 3-day avg of -$0.77/MW, with HE18 (+$0.20), HE14, and HE15 all showing repeatable positive DA spreads.

**Largest Negative Spreads (DA Offer Risk):** NSPIN carries the most significant DA offer risk — 3-day avg spread of **-$2.66/MW** with a catastrophic single-hour worst of **-$39.92/MW at HE22 on 10-26**. ECRS also flagged a severe -$18.64/MW at HE09 on 10-27. Both services show dangerous RT-over-DA outcomes in morning and late-evening hours; DA offers in NSPIN and ECRS during HE09 and HE22 should be avoided or minimized until these spreads normalize.

**Best Single AS Opportunity for Tomorrow's DA Offer:** Prioritize **REGDN at HE18** — the single most repeatable positive DA spread across all services and all hours ($+2.27/MW 3-day avg, peak $+5.74/MW on 10-26). The evening hour aligns with declining solar and load ramp-down when REGDN demand is structurally elevated and RT clearing tends to undershoot DA awards. File REGDN capacity at HE18 across eligible nodes (particularly JUNCTION_RN, TOYAH_RN, and HAMI_BESS_RN where DA-lean Sharpe signals already support DA commitment) before the 10:00 AM CT AS deadline.

---

## 7. ASSET AVAILABILITY

Asset availability data from PowerTools is currently unavailable due to the pending HTTP trigger endpoint configuration from IT. This is a **operational risk flag** — without confirmed availability data, dispatch recommendations in this report assume full fleet availability across all 32 nodes, which may not reflect actual unit commitment constraints, planned maintenance, or SOC limitations. Trading desk should manually confirm availability for the top-priority nodes (MAINLAND_RN, CEDRVALE_RN, SANDLAKE_RN, PAVLOV_BT_RN, JUNCTION_RN) before finalizing DA offers. **Escalate PowerTools integration to IT as high priority** — the inability to cross-reference outage data against dispatch signals is a commercial risk management gap.

---

## 8. FORWARD OPPORTUNITIES

**Opportunity 1 — West Texas RT Spike Capture (10-29 to 10-30, High Confidence):**
The near-certain precipitation across Midland/Lubbock/West Texas (99–100% precip probability) will suppress solar output through Friday morning, tightening the RT stack at West Texas nodes. CEDRVALE_RN, SANDLAKE_RN, COYOTSPR_RN, and FAULKNER_RN are structurally positioned to capture RT premiums given 5-day Sharpe signals of -0.45 to -0.46 and yesterday's RT premiums of $58–$75/MWh. Ensure these nodes are positioned for RT dispatch with minimal DA commitment in the 10-29 and 10-30 energy windows — this is the highest near-term revenue opportunity in the fleet.

**Opportunity 2 — JUNCTION_RN & TOYAH_RN DA Lock-In Before Regime Flip (10-29, Today):**
Both nodes carry positive Sharpe ratios, consistent DA premiums, and strong MCC support (JUNCTION +$77.88, TOYAH historically supported by ASHERT_CATARI1_1). With the West Texas precipitation system set to clear by 10-31 and wind/solar resuming, negative price risk at TOYAH may return — locking in DA prices today before RT normalizes captures the current DA premium window. File DA energy commitments at these nodes in today's 10:00 AM auction at market-reflective prices, with REGDN AS layered at HE18 for additional margin.

**Opportunity 3 — PAVLOV_BT_RN Congestion Arbitrage Monitoring (7–14 Day):**
PAVLOV_BT_RN's extraordinary MCC benefit of +$133.84/MWh and the BLESSI_PAVLOV1_1 constraint binding 12 hours at avg $141.33/MWh shadow price suggest a persistent structural congestion pattern on the Blessing-to-Pavlov path. If this constraint continues to bind through the weather event window (elevated transmission stress from load shifts during storm events), PAVLOV could sustain outsized nodal price separation from the hub. Monitor BLESSI_PAVLOV1_1 binding status daily and build a 7-day forward dispatch plan that maximizes RT discharge at PAVLOV during hours when the constraint is projected to bind — historically HE04 has been the peak binding hour, making overnight discharge at PAVLOV a potentially high-value strategy if SOC can be managed accordingly.

---

## 9. RISK FLAGS

**🚨 BLESSING Complex Constraint Persistence (Escalate Now):** The BLESSING_1382 constraint binding for **21 of 24 hours** with a $409.87/MWh peak shadow price is an extreme congestion event. A constraint at this persistence level may indicate infrastructure limitations (thermal rating, planned outage of a parallel path) that could persist for multiple days — if this recurs today, FTDUNCAN_RN's -$16.87/MWh MCC cost will compound into a multi-day settlement loss while CATARINA_B1, HOLCOMB_RN1, and MV_VALV4_RN continue to benefit. Trading desk should request ERCOT's constraint detail for BLESSING_1382 to determine if a planned outage is driving the sustained binding and whether the constraint is expected to clear this week.

**⚠️ NSPIN DA Offer Risk — HE22 Catastrophic Spread:** The -$39.92/MW RT-over-DA spread at HE22 for NSPIN on 10-26 represents a severe settlement risk for any node that cleared NSPIN in the DA market that hour. Combined with the -$18.64/MW ECRS spread at HE09 on 10-27, there is a clear pattern of late-evening and mid-morning hours where RT AS prices have blown through DA awards. Any DA NSPIN or ECRS offers filed for HE09 or HE22 slots should be reviewed immediately for open exposure.

**⚠️ PowerTools Outage Data Gap:** As flagged in Section 6, the absence of real-time asset availability data creates an unquantified operational risk. If any of the 10 spike nodes or top Sharpe-signal nodes are on forced or planned outage, today's dispatch strategy may be optimizing against unavailable units — a direct revenue loss and potential imbalance risk. This needs IT resolution before the next morning cycle.

**📋 Fleet RT Trend Acceleration Risk:** The 3-day ascending RT average ($22 → $42 → $57/MWh) combined with 10 spike nodes yesterday suggests the fleet is moving into a higher-volatility pricing regime ahead of the precipitation event. If today's weather-driven solar suppression produces a fleet RT average meaningfully above $57/MWh, nodes that committed heavily in DA (if any) will have underperformed — reinforcing the RT-bias strategy but also raising battery cycling and degradation considerations that asset management should monitor across the high-dispatch nodes.

---
